boxes.comments: The first word has an open u followed by a flattened n. In the second, the looped d, low e, and descending g are visible; the terminal r/e group is compressed. A detached final accent is not securely isolated, so degré/degre remains local. No following neighboring word is completed.

The central connected group is read égal/egal: a small initial loop, a long descending g, flattened a, and raised final l. No detached initial accent is secure. Two separate dark baseline marks follow; they are retained as two points, without extending them to three.
The large initial oval and long low tail are read On. In devrait, the d ascender, low e/v/r bodies, a rise, separate i dot, and terminal tall t are visible. No final punctuation is added.

The first word has a looped l and compressed e/s bodies, read les. The second has low initial bodies, a tall open ascender, and a compressed terminal return; relier is tentative. The word is retained whole under a local uncertainty rather than completed from syntax.
The main g has an upper oval and a long lower return. Its lower-right i has a detached dot, and a smaller closed oval lies farther down/right, read subscript zero. No bar or extra mark is supplied.

Full formula read. The initial letter is V followed by a slash. The g has nested i and zero; its small raised angular mark has several short arms, tentatively star, and remains uncertain. The left parenthesized term has J with lower f. The relation has a wavy upper stroke and one straight lower bar. The A has heavy retracing and an additional curved inner stroke; ordinary/double-stroke alphabet assignment remains uncertain. The right denominator has J with nested g, i, zero, a plus, and J with lower f, followed by the closing parenthesis. The partial curve above A belongs to the clipped neighboring line and is excluded.

A horizontal dash precedes a small oval and a flattened second body. The latter admits u/n, and a grave accent is not securely isolated; ou/où/on remains unresolved. The following separate sign has a short left arm and a taller curved right arm, read nu. Material beyond this complete group is excluded.

The raised addition ends in a separate comma. Its prefix is compressed enough that sous/ss cannot be separated securely; an explicit hyphen precedes schémas, whose h ascender and raised accent are visible. A long curved attachment runs below the addition and drops between the baseline des and f(S); it is recorded as an insertion leader, not an underline or parenthesis. The baseline f and parenthesized S are retained as the anchor. The following et meets the right edge and is not completed. A clipped upper-left neighboring stroke is excluded.

Complete g with lower i and smaller zero, followed by an opening parenthesis, a large looped S, and a closing parenthesis. The i dot is dark and detached; the zero has an enclosed counter. No following word is supplied.
Capital J has an upper flourish and a long lower loop; its following e has a small closed upper loop and right return. Read Je, with no additional punctuation.

The first tall l and separate apostrophe are followed by hom, with a tall h and very low o/m bodies. No distinct terminal stop is visible in this crop, so the abbreviation remains unexpanded and without a period.
The p stem descends well below the compressed a/r bodies. The separate sign has a left stem with a lower hook and an upward right arm, read mu. Full central group par mu retained.

The left letter has a top bar and a lower hook/return, read J, with a small looped ell below/right. The right node is T with lower ell and a raised serifed I. The connector has a long shaft and only a short downward terminal cap; a complete two-wing head is not securely separated. Plain stroke/right arrow is retained as a local doubt, with both endpoints included. No comma outside the frozen box is added.
A dotted i is followed by a smaller closed oval at a lower level, read zero. A distinct final dark point follows the index. Read i subscript zero and period.

The left sign has a short slanted left arm and a long curved right arm, read nu. Two separate parallel equality bars follow. The final digit has a diagonal top entry, heavily retraced vertical stem, and long bottom foot, read 1. No outside comma is supplied.

Le and the body sequence fait are recoverable. The f has a tall upper loop and a large lower return, followed by a densely overlaid oval cluster, dotted i, and tall final t. Several low crossings overlap the f/a area and the e of Le; their separation into cancellation and letter returns is not secure. The state of fait is therefore left locally uncertain between live and canceled; no older word or revision chronology is invented. Clipped neighboring material at the upper-left is excluded.

The central word reads premiers. A single horizontal stroke begins beneath the terminal r/s area and extends beyond the word; its observed scope is encoded on rs. Beneath it is a dense crossed/retraced one-glyph-sized cluster that cannot be read securely, retained as deleted illegible ink. Below that cluster is a curved question-mark/2-like form followed by an exclamation-like vertical mark with a dark lower point; ?!/2! remains unresolved. The p descender meets the bottom crop edge, while the central word bodies are complete.
Tall looped l, separate upper apostrophe, and hom are visible. A distinct separate dark terminal point follows the m. Read the abbreviation l'hom. without expansion.

Full formula and both connector ends are included. Each pi has a lower 1. The first parenthesized sign has an arch and a descending right leg, read eta. The connector has one small pointed/looped right terminal head. Both U forms have open upper entries. The relation has a wavy upper stroke and a lower straight bar. The final U has a lower s. All three parenthesis pairs are visible; no terminal punctuation is added. Clipped marks at the top belong to the neighboring annotation and are excluded.

A crossed initial sign has a long left stem and an arched right part, tentatively mu, and is encoded as deleted. The following indexed letter has a tall stem, short upper-right branch or crossbar, and lower-right stroke; k/K/f remains local because the branch and crossing are overlaid. Its i dot and smaller lower zero are visible. The following composition sign is an open-centered circle. Inside the parentheses are mu, a low point, dotted i and looped d, then a lower T. The low point is retained literally as a period. A separate comma follows the closing parenthesis. Full central formula is retained without inferring a replacement chronology.

The indexed letter has a tall left stem and two right branches; the letter body supports k/K, with case unresolved. The lower i has a detached dot and the smaller zero has a visible counter. The following complete word est has an initial loop and terminal tall crossed return. A tiny isolated point near the upper edge is not securely attached to the indexed letter and is not promoted to a diacritic.

The three-line margin note was rotated clockwise 35 degrees before enlargement. Ceci, doit, the word body etre, independant, and de la valeur de nu are read. The circumflex and acute accent are not independently isolated securely, so accent alternatives remain local. The final sign has the same short-left/tall-curved-right outline read as nu in the page. No terminal punctuation is supplied. Large clipped main-body strokes along the rotated right boundary and below the note are excluded; they are not read as punctuation or completed words.
Separate lower-left foliation comprises two crossed 7 forms. Read 77 and encode as a margin number; page edge is visible below.
